title: issue53843/fix53849 ingest writer lifecycle leak on cancel

payload.validation_scope: deterministic root-cause boundary replay of concurrent UnregisterEngines; full SQL/cluster cancel flow remains a separate E2E oracle
payload.user_symptom: ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS during ADD INDEX can panic the DDL worker with close-of-closed-channel style cleanup failure and leak ingest writers
payload.next_step: turn this root-boundary oracle into a reusable fault-injection harness that can drive the full ADD INDEX cancel flow

provenance.source: local historical worktrees plus issue 53843 metadata

name: Concurrent unregister closes each ingest engine exactly once

payload.contract: If two cleanup/cancel paths call UnregisterEngines for the same live ingest backend context, the same opened engine must not be closed or cleaned more than once.
minimal_observation: first UnregisterEngines enters CloseEngine and is held before openedEngine is nulled
second UnregisterEngines runs in the overlap window
close_calls must remain 1 until the first cleanup is released
after both complete, close_calls=1, cleanup_calls=1, remaining_engines=0

red_signature.message: second unregister closed the same engine while the first unregister was still in progress

blind_spots: Does not by itself prove the complete SQL ADD INDEX + ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS user flow
Does not count live writer leaks after all possible ingest phases

rationale: the exact historical fix serializes UnregisterEngines, so the narrow oracle should verify duplicate cleanup rather than only broad no-leak behavior

source_anchors: pkg/ddl/ingest/engine_mgr.go:103-108 has no synchronization around bc.engines cleanup

evidence.failure_message: second unregister closed the same engine while the first unregister was still in progress
evidence.oracle: close_calls must never exceed 1 while the first unregister is still in progress
log_lines: issue53843-vulnerable-red-go121.log:8 second unregister closed the same engine while the first unregister was still in progress

lessons.selector_worked: LIFECYCLE_EXACTLY_ONCE found the bug by forcing overlapping cleanup paths at the resource registry boundary
lessons.method_note: The fast path was not a performance fast path; it was a missing serialization assumption over a mutable resource map. The AI loop should ask which P check makes the system believe Q: here P=len/map iteration over live engines, Q=cleanup can run once without external serialization.
lessons.scope_caveat: This is strong root-cause evidence, not a full cluster SQL symptom replay.

source_anchors: pkg/ddl/ingest/engine_mgr.go:105-119 locks unregisterMu and returns when engines is empty

evidence.oracle: same as RED run; the fix prevents concurrent duplicate cleanup

lessons.fix_shape: Serialize cleanup over the backend context and make subsequent unregister idempotent when the engine map is empty.
lessons.method_note: Once the red cell appears, the fix selector is visible: protect the single ownership transition, not individual close calls.
lessons.scope_caveat: The broad no-leak-after-cancel oracle should remain partially open until exercised through SQL/cluster DDL cancel.
